summary:
This joint resolution invokes the Congressional Review Act (CRA), codified at chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code (5 U.S.C. §§ 801–808), to disapprove and nullify a rule issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The operative mechanism is the CRA's expedited disapproval procedure. Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 802, the resolution provides that Congress disapproves the identified agency action and that "such rule shall have no force or effect." Enactment would trigger the consequences of 5 U.S.C. § 801(b)(1)—rendering the rule ineffective—and 5 U.S.C. § 801(b)(2), which bars the agency from reissuing the rule in substantially the same form, or issuing a new substantially similar rule, absent subsequent statutory authorization.

The specific agency action targeted is SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 121, published at 87 Fed. Reg. 21015 (April 11, 2022). SAB 121 sets forth interpretive guidance regarding the accounting treatment for obligations to safeguard crypto-assets held for platform users, including balance-sheet recognition.

The resolution incorporates, as a predicate, a letter opinion of the Government Accountability Office dated October 31, 2023, printed in the Congressional Record at pages S5310–5312 (November 1, 2023), which concluded that SAB 121 constitutes a "rule" within the meaning of chapter 8 of title 5. This determination is significant because it establishes that the bulletin—styled as staff-level accounting guidance rather than a promulgated rule—falls within the CRA's definition of a rule and is therefore subject to congressional review. The GAO opinion effectively addressed the threshold jurisdictional question of whether the submission requirement of 5 U.S.C. § 801(a)(1)(A) was implicated and whether the measure is reviewable under the Act.

The resolution contains no severability clause, effective-date provision, sunset, authorization of appropriations, or appropriation, consistent with the standard form of a CRA disapproval resolution. It effects neither an amendment nor a repeal of existing U.S. Code text; its sole legal effect operates through the CRA framework to void the identified rule and to impose the § 801(b)(2) reissuance bar.

The document reflects the resolution's status as passed by the House of Representatives on May 8, 2024, and received in the Senate on May 9, 2024. As a joint resolution, it requires passage by both chambers and presentment to the President under Article I, Section 7 to take effect, unless a veto is overridden.
